A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 25-page paper, including Appendices A–F. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that the paper content is identical; the visible difference is the first-page arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports theoretical definitions, constructions, and proofs, including those in Appendices D–F. It contains no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes; empirical observations are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same theoretical content and appendices. It adds no original empirical outcomes; the figures summarize concepts and theoretical relationships.

M1.justification: The circuit constructions in Section 4 and Appendices D and F, and the gradient-based training procedure in Algorithm 1, are identical.

E1.justification: Neither version reports datasets or tasks actually used in empirical training or evaluation. The DLP-based and constructed supervised-learning tasks remain unchanged theoretical examples.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The theoretical comparisons involving DLP kernels, hardware-efficient ansätze, and classical learners are unchanged.

E3.justification: No experimental evaluation protocol is reported in either version. The learning-task specifications, optimization objectives, and initialization assumptions used in the theoretical constructions are identical.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or error analyses are added or removed. The supplementary discussions of existing models and gradient-based trainability in Appendices C and E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Variance and probability statements belong to the same unchanged theoretical definitions and arguments.

E6.justification: No numerical results or qualitative findings change. Both versions report the same theoretical outcomes in Section 4 and Figure 3, without empirical performance results.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–4, Proposition 1, Theorem 3, Corollaries 2 and 4, and all accompanying assumptions, equations, derivations, and appendix proofs are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: formalizing trainability and dequantization and establishing the existence of gradient-based trainable, non-dequantizable variational QML models.

C2.justification: Section 5 and the appendices retain the same interpretations and limitations, including task-dependent definitions, contrived circuit constructions, easy learning with solutions embedded in the architecture, and unresolved practical relevance.

D1.justification: The algorithmic and circuit-construction details are identical. Neither version adds implementation settings, hardware or runtime measurements, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: Section 3, Appendix C, and the reference list are unchanged, including the positioning relative to Liu et al. (2021), Gyurik and Dunjko (2023), and Cerezo et al. (2023).

P1.justification: The first-page margin stamp changes from arXiv:2406.07072v2, dated 12 February 2025, to v3, dated 8 July 2025. All paper prose, terminology, headings, and main-text/appendix organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3, Algorithm 1, captions, equations, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–25 render identically, and the first-page body is also identical; the margin stamp update does not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, proofs, discussion, references, and complete appendices are identical. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and adding its self-link does not materially change correctness, clarity, evidential support, or reproducibility.
